fixture.interpretation: In fixture mode the single_call, agent and agent_single_inspection arms replay hand-written replies with planted failures. Those rows check the tools, policy and grader; they are not model results. The rule_table arm calls no model, so its rows are real measurements of that baseline.

limitations: Six development and ten held-out incidents on three original toy solvers, written by the author together with the rule table. Useful for testing behaviour, too small to rank models.
The rule table was written with knowledge of the fault types, so it is a strong scripted reference rather than a naive baseline.
The simulated approver approves any tested patch whose checks pass; it does not model a human reviewer.
The subprocess runner enforces a time limit everywhere and a memory limit only on POSIX.
There is no production integration: no scheduler, cluster, file system or real code.
Each live run is ten held-out incidents with one or two runs per arm at temperature 0: an exploratory sample, not a ranking. v1 and v2 use different incident families, so their rows are not paired.

reproduce.fixture: python -m scientific_recovery_agent evaluate --config configs/recovery_fixture.yaml && python -m scientific_recovery_agent report
reproduce.live: python -m scientific_recovery_agent evaluate --config configs/recovery_live.yaml --require-live && python -m scientific_recovery_agent report
